transcript.text: When someone asks for a discount, they
don't usually say, "Hey, give me a
discount." They usually say, "Hey, could
you work on this price a little bit?"
Or, "Hey, could you do this for a little
less?" And when someone says that, I
just usually respond with, "I could do
it for more." And I swear, it just
completely reframes the question of
like, "Well, what are we talking about
here?" And I have used that to get out
of the whole negotiation of this because
whenever someone's asking for a
discount, they've already decided to
buy. They're trying to get it for less.
And the reason that it works so well is
that it creates a negative anchor. So,
basically, they've already said yes
mentally here. It's just a little bit
uncomfortable. And as soon as you anchor
above by saying, "I could do it for
more," typically, they'll just say like,
"Shoot, I don't want the price to get
away. I'll buy." And whenever I say
that, tone matters a lot, right? So, if
you just say like, "I could do it for
more," like, yeah, of course no one's
going to be like, "What? This guy's a
dick." You're like, "I could do it for
more." Like, it sounds a lot different,
and that's what ultimately closes the
sale. You'll get a laugh, and you'll get
a deal.
